what: NRG Energy sells electricity and natural gas directly to about eight million residential customers and to businesses, and owns power plants to supply much of it. It also sells smart home security through Vivint.
customers: Households and businesses buying retail electricity and gas, data centres, and wholesale power markets.
money: retail electricity and generation in the Texas market
retail and generation in other regional markets
moat: Owning both the generation and the retail customers, so the two hedge each other naturally when wholesale power prices spike.
risks: Debt of about $23 billion against almost no cash
Power prices are volatile and Texas winter storms have caused large losses before
Net margin of about 3% reflects commodity exposure
Buying a large generation portfolio adds integration risk
opportunities: Analysts see large upside, with a median target well above the current price
Data centre demand in Texas is raising power prices and the value of existing plants
Vivint subscriptions add recurring revenue unrelated to power
watch: Any power agreements with data centre customers, and Texas forward power prices.
